content.text: Maven is a build automation tool used primarily for Java projects. It helps manage project dependencies, build processes, and project configurations.

items: Installation: Download and install Maven on your system, and configure it with a JAVA_HOME variable to ensure it works properly.

content.text: Once Maven is installed, you can use it from the command line to build and deploy the Infycart application.

items: Clean Command: To clean any previous build artifacts, run: mvn clean This command removes the target/ directory and any compiled files from previous builds.
Compile Command: To compile the Java classes, use: mvn compile This command compiles the source code in the src/main/java directory.
Package Command: To package the application into a WAR file: mvn package This command generates a .war file in the target/ directory.
Deploy Command: To deploy the application to a Tomcat server, run: mvn clean install tomcat7:run After deployment, access the application through the browser at http://localhost:9090.
Importing: To import a Maven project in Eclipse, go to File → Import... → Existing Maven Projects and select the pom.xml file.
Running Maven Goals: After importing, use the Maven toolbar to execute goals like clean, install, etc., or use the terminal inside Eclipse.
Importing: Open IntelliJ, select File → Open, and choose the project folder containing the pom.xml.
Running Maven Goals: Use the Maven tool window in IntelliJ to execute Maven commands and manage dependencies.
Build Profiles: A build profile is a set of configuration values that override the default Maven configurations. It helps in managing different environments (e.g., development, production).
Example:  These can be configured within pom.xml using <profiles> and <profile> nodes.
Setting Profiles:

Using Profiles:
Use the command: mvn clean install -P<profile-id> Example: mvn clean install -Pdev
Super POM: The default configuration for Maven, which includes repository and plugin configurations. It is inherited by all projects but can be customized.
Effective POM: The combination of the Super POM and the project's specific pom.xml. This is generated on-the-fly and shows the actual configuration Maven uses.

content.text: Dependencies in Maven have various scopes that control their availability and lifespan during the build process.

items:
compile: Default scope. Dependencies are available during compilation, testing, and runtime. These dependencies are propagated to dependent projects. <dependency>
  <groupId>log4j</groupId>
  <artifactId>log4j</artifactId>
  <version>1.2.17</version>
  <scope>compile</scope>
</dependency>
provided: Dependencies required during compilation and testing but are provided by the container or environment at runtime (e.g., servlet APIs). <dependency>
  <groupId>javax.servlet</groupId>
  <artifactId>javax.servlet-api</artifactId>
  <version>4.0.0</version>
  <scope>provided</scope>
</dependency>
runtime: Dependencies not needed for compilation but required at runtime and during testing. <dependency>
  <groupId>mysql</groupId>
  <artifactId>mysql-connector-java</artifactId>
  <version>5.1.10</version>
  <scope>runtime</scope>
</dependency>
test: Dependencies needed only for compiling and running tests. <dependency>
  <groupId>junit</groupId>
  <artifactId>junit</artifactId>
  <version>4.12</version>
  <scope>test</scope>
</dependency>
system: Dependencies that are provided by the user and specified with an absolute path. These are not retrieved from a repository.
import: Used for importing BOM (Bill of Materials) files in dependency management.

content.text: Maven allows managing multi-module projects where each module has its own POM file but shares a common parent POM. The parent POM handles the shared configurations like dependency versions, plugin versions, and properties.

items: Example:
Maven plugins can be configured and customized in the pom.xml to perform specific actions at different phases of the build lifecycle.
By default, tomcat plugin listens to port 8080.
Just in case, if you wish tomcat to use port 8081, then the behavior of tomcat plugin's run goal can be customized using the following configuration: tomcat:run -Dmaven.tomcat.port = 8181
Through command prompt: mvn tomcat:run -Dmaven.tomcat.port = 8181 where mvn : command for running Maven
D : represents define
Dname = value : to pass parameters to Maven goals(maven.tomcat.port - in this case)

Example: <plugin>
  <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
  <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
  <version>3.8.1</version>
  <executions>
    <execution>
      <phase>compile</phase>
      <goals>
        <goal>compile</goal>
      </goals>
    </execution>
  </executions>
</plugin>

content.text: By customizing plugin goals, you can fine-tune the build process to fit your project's requirements.
